docs.title: Killah
docs.text:
Killah is a writing app for macOS with a built-in AI assistant called lil Pushkin. lil Pushkin is a language model, the same kind of software that powers ChatGPT or Claude, and it runs directly on your Mac. Everything you write stays on your computer.

Because the model lives on your Mac, you pay for Killah once and use it forever. Instead of a subscription, per-word charges, or sudden price changes, Killah gives you a local tool that keeps working.

docs.title: What you can do with Killah
docs.text:
• Finish your thought. As you type, lil Pushkin predicts what might come next and shows the guess in grey after your cursor. Press Tab to take it, keep typing to ignore it.
  • Rewrite a passage. Select a sentence, describe the change in plain words, such as shorter, more formal, or turn into a question, and get a new version.
  • Dictate. Speak into the microphone and watch your words land at the cursor. The audio stays on your Mac.
  • Write in your own voice. Point Killah at something you have already written, and it will steer future suggestions toward your vocabulary and rhythm.

Works on Apple Silicon Macs

Killah needs macOS 26 Tahoe or newer and an M1 or later chip. The model is too heavy for Intel Macs to run smoothly.

docs.title: About
docs.text: Killah is a writing app for macOS. It was made by Vladislav Kalinichenko.

docs.title: Why Killah works this way
docs.text:
Most AI writing tools send your text to a remote server, have it processed by a language model there, and send the result back. That setup has two practical costs for you. Your drafts pass through a company outside your control, and the company has to bill you every month to keep its servers running.

Killah takes the opposite approach. The language model, nicknamed lil Pushkin, is downloaded to your Mac on first launch and runs there from then on. Your writing stays on your computer, and the price is a one-time purchase. Instead of a subscription you have to keep paying for, Killah stays available as long as your Mac keeps working, even years from now while offline.

Running a language model locally costs compute instead of money. Killah uses your chip and memory to do what a cloud service would otherwise bill you for. That is why your Mac warms up and the fans spin during generation, the same way they do when you run a demanding video game.

docs.title: A note on the name
docs.text: "lil Pushkin" is a nickname for the language model. When the docs say "lil Pushkin suggests" or "lil Pushkin answers", they mean the model produced that output.

docs.title: License
docs.text: Killah is a one-time purchase. You pay once and keep using the app forever. Instead of a subscription or monthly charge, Killah uses lil Pushkin directly on your Mac.

docs.title: Trial period
docs.text: A fresh installation starts with a free trial. During the trial, every feature works exactly as it would with a paid license, so you can see how suggestions, rewriting, voice input, and style memory fit into your writing before committing. The Welcome screen shows how many days are left.

docs.title: Activating a license
docs.text:
1. Buy a license key on the Killah website.
  2. Open the license screen in the app. It appears automatically when the trial ends, and you can also reach it from the Welcome screen.
  3. Enter your key in the format KILLAH-XXXX-XXXX and click Validate Key.
  4. When the key is accepted, the license is active on this Mac.

Your key is tied to your purchase. Keep it somewhere safe, because you will need it again if you reinstall macOS or move to a new Mac.

docs.title: When the trial ends
docs.text:
If the trial expires before you enter a license, Killah still opens and you can still read and edit your documents. The AI features, including autocomplete, rewrite, voice input, and style memory, are paused until you enter a valid key.

Buy a license key on Boosty.

docs.title: lil Pushkin
docs.text: lil Pushkin is the AI assistant inside Killah. Technically, it is a language model, the same kind of software that powers ChatGPT or Claude, but it is small enough to run on your Mac and is packaged to work offline. Everything lil Pushkin reads, writes, or hears happens on your computer.

docs.title: What this means for you
docs.text:
Most AI tools today live on a website. You open a browser, type into a box, and somewhere a company's server processes your request. You pay monthly for that access, and the moment you stop paying, the tool is gone.

Killah works differently. lil Pushkin runs directly on your Mac as a piece of software you download and own instead of a service you rent. You buy Killah once and it is yours permanently. Instead of subscriptions, price increases, or account access problems, the program stays with you the way a book on your shelf stays with you.

Privacy and offline use follow from the same fact: because the model runs on your hardware, your drafts stay on the computer, and you can write offline.

docs.title: How lil Pushkin helps you write
docs.text:
• Autocomplete. While you type, lil Pushkin looks at the last few paragraphs and guesses what might come next. If the guess is plausible, it appears in grey after the cursor. Press Tab to take it.
  • Rewrite. Select a sentence or paragraph, tell lil Pushkin how you want it changed, and it produces a new version. Instructions can be as short as "shorter" or "friendlier".
  • Dictate. Speak into the microphone and lil Pushkin transcribes your voice into text at the cursor.
  • Style memory. Point lil Pushkin at a document you have already written, and it will steer future suggestions toward your vocabulary and rhythm.

docs.title: How prediction works
docs.text: A language model reads a chunk of text and estimates, for every possible next word, how likely that word is to follow. Killah gives lil Pushkin the text around your cursor and asks for the most probable continuation.

docs.title: The model files
docs.text:
The first time you launch Killah, lil Pushkin has to be downloaded. The files are roughly 7 to 8 GB. This is a one-time step; once the files are on disk, Killah loads them into memory each time it starts.

You can remove or re-download the files at any time from Settings → lil Pushkin. Removing them frees disk space. The next time you use a feature that needs the model, Killah will ask to download it again.

Offline after the first download

After the initial download, lil Pushkin works fully offline.

docs.title: The smart caret
docs.text: The smart caret is the red cursor that follows where you are typing. It is the fastest way to reach lil Pushkin from the keyboard, and it puts every AI action right at the place you are working on instead of behind a menu.

docs.title: Opening the control panel
docs.text:
Click the caret to open a compact panel with three actions.

Action What it does Record Starts voice dictation. Speak into the microphone, click again to stop, and Killah inserts the transcription at the cursor. Ask lil Pushkin Opens a text field. Type a short instruction and lil Pushkin rewrites your selection or continues from the cursor. Autocomplete Asks for a suggestion right now, instead of waiting for one to appear on its own.

docs.title: Inline suggestions
docs.text:
While you type, Killah asks lil Pushkin every few words whether it has a good continuation. When it does, the continuation appears in grey immediately after your cursor.

  • Press Tab to accept it.
  • Press Esc to dismiss it.
  • Keep typing to ignore it. The grey text disappears the moment you go a different way.

Suggestions are produced in the background, so you can keep typing while lil Pushkin thinks. If lil Pushkin finishes a guess after you have already moved on, that guess is quietly dropped.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text: See Keyboard shortcuts for every caret-related key, including the two shortcuts that nudge the next suggestion toward a safer or more adventurous tone.

docs.title: Style personalization
docs.text: Killah can adapt autocomplete, continuation, rewrite, and cleaned-up dictation to the general way you write. It learns from all .txt and .rtf files in the Documents folder, then creates one style instruction and one fixed steering vector. Source passages are not copied into generation prompts.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
At launch, Killah compares each file's content fingerprint with its saved SwiftData record. New and changed files are prepared; unchanged files are reused; deleted files are removed from the profile. Saving a document inside Killah triggers the same comparison for that file, while merely activating the app does nothing.

If preparation is interrupted, the unfinished record returns to pending and resumes after the model becomes available. The last complete profile stays active while a replacement is built, so background work never leaves writing half-personalized.

docs.title: Large collections
docs.text: Documents larger than the model context are analyzed in bounded chunks. When the complete collection is larger than the style-analysis budget, Killah shuffles complete samples into that budget instead of silently truncating every file at the same position.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Use personalization applies or bypasses the current profile everywhere.
  • Refresh personalization rechecks the Documents folder immediately.
  • Changing the Documents folder discards the old corpus identity and builds from the new folder.

The bottom progress bar is shared with model loading, so it shows the highest-priority active operation without overlapping indicators.

docs.title: Voice input
docs.text:
Voice input turns what you say into text in the document. It is useful when your hands are tired, when you think faster than you type, or when you are away from the keyboard and want to capture an idea before it slips away.

Like the rest of Killah, it runs on your Mac. The audio stays on the computer, so you can dictate private notes while keeping the recording local.

docs.title: How to dictate
docs.text:
1. Place the cursor where you want the text to land.
  2. Click the red caret and choose Record.
  3. Speak at a normal pace while the status line reads Listening….
  4. Stop the recording. Killah transcribes the audio and inserts the result at the cursor.

You can dictate punctuation out loud. Say "comma", "period", or "new paragraph" where you want the mark, and the transcriber inserts the correct symbol.

docs.title: How the transcription works
docs.text:
Voice input uses NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 through the native MLX Swift runtime. Parakeet streams partial text into the prompt while you speak, then replaces it with the finalized transcript when recording ends; all inference stays on the Mac.

Audio lives only in a short working buffer during processing. Once the text appears in the document, the recording is gone.

docs.title: Getting cleaner transcripts
docs.text:
• Record in a quiet room. Background noise is the single biggest source of errors.
  • Speak in complete sentences. Parakeet uses surrounding words to resolve ambiguous fragments, so a complete phrase usually produces a cleaner final transcript.
  • For names, acronyms, and technical terms, slow down and pronounce them clearly. Rare words are harder for the model than common ones.

Microphone access

The first time you record, macOS asks for microphone permission. Killah turns the microphone on only while you are actively recording and turns it off again the moment you stop.

docs.title: System requirements
docs.text:
Killah runs a language model locally, so it needs a Mac that can handle real compute. Apple Silicon machines can run it smoothly enough for everyday writing. Intel Macs are too slow for this workload in practice.

Requirement Minimum macOS macOS 26 Tahoe or newer Chip Apple Silicon, starting with M1 Memory 8 GB. With 16 GB, suggestions arrive noticeably faster. Free disk space Around 8 GB for the model files

docs.title: Installing the app
docs.text:
1. Download the latest .dmg from the releases page.
  2. Open the disk image and drag Killah.app into Applications.
  3. Launch Killah from Spotlight or the Applications folder.

docs.title: Letting macOS open the app
docs.text:
Killah is currently distributed outside the App Store, so macOS treats it as an app from an unidentified developer on first launch. You may see a warning that asks you to stop before opening the app, or says that it may contain malware. This is a standard Gatekeeper notice for apps distributed this way.

To open Killah anyway:

  1. Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security.
  2. Scroll to the Security section. You will see a message that reads "Killah" was blocked to protect your Mac.
  3. Click Open Anyway.
  4. macOS will ask once more to confirm. Click Open.

After this, Killah opens normally on every subsequent launch.

docs.title: First launch
docs.text:
The first time Killah opens, it asks to download lil Pushkin, the language model that powers autocomplete, rewrite, and voice input. Because the model runs on your Mac instead of a server, its files have to live on your disk. The download is about 7 to 8 GB and only happens once. You can start writing as soon as it finishes.

The files are saved in Killah's application support directory. Later launches load them from disk instead of downloading them again.

The chip will work hard

Running a language model is a lot like running a demanding video game. The M-series chip loads the GPU and Neural Engine at full capacity, and on laptops the fans come on. This is expected during autocomplete, rewrite, and style memory. When you stop using these features, the Mac cools down again within a few seconds.

docs.title: License
docs.text: Killah needs an active trial or a valid license key to run. See License for how the trial works and how to enter a key.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page walks through the four things you need to know to start writing with Killah. It takes about five minutes.

docs.title: 1. Create a document
docs.text: Click New Document on the Welcome screen, or press Cmd + N from anywhere in the app. Documents are plain text files stored in the folder set under Settings → Documents. You can move them around in Finder like any other file.

docs.title: 2. Write and read the grey text
docs.text:
Type as you normally would. Every few words, Killah asks lil Pushkin for a guess at what might come next. When the guess looks plausible, it appears in grey right after your cursor.

  • Press Tab to take the suggestion.
  • Press Esc to dismiss it.
  • Keep typing to ignore it. The grey text disappears as soon as you go a different way, and a new guess may arrive shortly after.

docs.title: 3. Use the smart caret
docs.text:
Click the red caret at your cursor to open a small panel. From there you can:

  • Start a voice recording with Record.
  • Open an instruction field with Ask lil Pushkin to rewrite the current selection or continue from the cursor.

For details, see The smart caret.

docs.title: 4. Teach Killah your style if you want to
docs.text:
Put examples of your writing in the Documents folder and leave Settings → Personalization → Use personalization enabled. Killah prepares changed files in the background and builds one transferable style profile for new topics; the progress bar at the bottom tells you when that work is running.

For how the feature works, see Style memory.

Keep writing

Suggestions are produced in the background. Killah lets you keep typing while lil Pushkin is thinking, so you can always just keep going.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Open the settings window with Cmd + ,.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text: The editor theme follows your macOS appearance setting automatically. When your Mac is in dark mode, Killah is dark. When it is in light mode, Killah is light. The app uses the system theme instead of its own separate theme setting.

docs.title: Documents
docs.text: Sets the folder where new documents are saved. Click Change folder… to choose a different location or Reset to default to go back. Files you already have on disk stay where they are; only documents created after the change use the new folder.

docs.title: Editor
docs.text:
Autocomplete automatically. When the switch is on, lil Pushkin offers suggestions as you type. When it is off, you get suggestions only when you press Tab or open the smart caret. Turning it off is useful on older Macs, or when you want fewer interruptions during a first draft.

Additional writing instructions. Adds your own system-level direction after Killah's built-in writing rules in autocomplete, continuation, rewrite, and cleaned-up dictation. Changing this text invalidates the shared prompt cache, so the next generation rebuilds that prefix once.

docs.title: lil Pushkin
docs.text:
Shows whether the language model files are on your disk and lets you manage them.

Status What it means lil Pushkin is at home All model files are present. Every AI feature is ready to use. N models need to be downloaded Some files are missing. Click Download models to fetch them. Downloading lil Pushkin… A download is in progress. Progress is shown next to the label.

Click Delete lil Pushkin to remove the files and free up disk space. You can re-download them later at any time. Your documents and settings are left alone.

docs.title: Personalization
docs.text:
Controls one style profile built from the text and RTF files in the Documents folder. Killah compares file fingerprints when the app starts and when an app-owned document is saved; unchanged files reuse their prepared summaries instead of being indexed again.

The status row shows whether the profile is ready, being updated, or waiting for the language model. Refresh personalization performs the same reconciliation on demand. Turning personalization off cancels background preparation and generations use only the built-in and optional user instructions.

docs.title: Suggestions
docs.text:
Key What it does Tab Accept the current suggestion. If the line is empty, ask lil Pushkin for one. Esc Dismiss the current suggestion. Cmd + → Regenerate the suggestion with a more adventurous tone. Cmd + ← Regenerate the suggestion with a more cautious tone.

The arrow shortcuts only affect the next regeneration. Your default style stays the same.

docs.title: Documents
docs.text: Key What it does Cmd + N Create a new document. Cmd + O Open an existing document from disk. Cmd + S Save. Autosave is always on, so you rarely need this.

docs.title: Formatting
docs.text: Key What it does Cmd + B Bold Cmd + I Italic Cmd + U Underline Cmd + Shift + X Strikethrough

docs.title: Creating a document
docs.text: Press Cmd + N or click New Document on the Welcome screen. New documents are saved as plain text in the folder chosen under Settings → Documents, so you can open them in any other editor or sync them through iCloud or Dropbox.

docs.title: Opening and managing documents
docs.text: Recent documents appear on the Welcome screen, grouped by date. To open another file, press Cmd + O and pick it in the file dialog. To change where new documents are saved, use Settings → Documents. Files already on disk stay where they are.

docs.title: Formatting
docs.text:
Killah keeps formatting minimal so the editor stays focused on writing. It gives you the four inline formats below instead of headings, lists, or paragraph styles.

Format Shortcut Bold Cmd + B Italic Cmd + I Underline Cmd + U Strikethrough Cmd + Shift + X

docs.title: Autosave
docs.text: Every change is written to disk shortly after you type it, so even a sudden shutdown should only cost a word or two. Instead of a manual save step or an unsaved-changes marker, Killah keeps the file current in the background. Cmd + S is accepted as a harmless shortcut for people who have the key in muscle memory.
